body:
Owner-requested GitHub issue https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/497; parallel execution requested 2026-10-03.

## Problem
`corvint-tasks dispatch` has static caps (`globalCap`, per-role `cap`). When the host is saturated the dispatcher keeps launching workers, queue mutations slow to minutes (see #494), sessions die on claim/heartbeat timeouts, and every timeout wastes a session and can charge a retry. The operator can only lower the caps by hand and reload, which cannot track load that changes hour to hour.

Observed (main-32aa5a3, one 10-core macOS host, ~11 concurrent OpenCode workers plus a Docker VM): load average 50-170 on 10 CPUs, swap 67-70%, 12 of 23 worker sessions in one hour lost to claim/heartbeat timeouts.

## Request
Native, optional host-pressure throttle in the dispatch config, e.g.
```json
"pressure": {"loadPerCpuHigh": 5, "loadPerCpuCritical": 8, "swapHigh": 0.8, "swapCritical": 0.9,
             "calmLoadPerCpu": 3.5, "calmSwap": 0.7, "ticksToChange": 2,
             "levelCaps": {"1": 5, "2": 3}, "exempt": ["pinned"]}
```
- Sample load/swap each tick, apply hysteresis, and cap NEW launches of non-exempt roles at the level cap. Running workers are never stopped; pinned/critical-path tickets and review/integration roles stay exempt.
- Show the level, inputs and held tickets in `dispatch status` and as an event (`throttled`).

## Workaround in use
A steward script computes the level and `workState` emits `hold-load` for excess authoring tickets. This works but duplicates logic that belongs next to the launch decision.
